cell.label: Patient with suspected influenza (fever, cough and/or myalgias); presentation within 48 hours of illness onset?
Further evaluation guided by relationship to flu season.
∼2% pretest probability of influenza: consider rapid flu test only if flu, otherwise likely due to severity of symptoms or recent exposure.
5%-10% pretest probability of flu: order rapid flu test.
1%-3% probability of flu: supportive treatment with adequate hydration, analgesics, and followup.
49%-67% probability of flu; initiate antiviral medication.
30%-50% pretest probability of flu: consider empiric therapy with antiviral medication vs. rapid flu test; result if flu test chosen?
11%-22% probability of flu: supportive treatment with adequate hydration, analgesics, and followup.
89%-95% probability of flu: initiate antiviral medication.
Supportive treatment with analgesics, adequate hydration, and follow-up; CXR to rule out pneumonia if lower respiratory tract symptoms.

footnotes.footnote: Data from Ebell MH. Diagnosing and treating patients with suspected influenza. Am Fam Physician 2005;72:1789–1792. Rothberg MB, Bellantonio S, Rose DN. Management of influenza in adults older than 65 years of age: cost-effectiveness of rapid testing and antiviral therapy. Ann Intern Med 2003;139:321–329.
